t:
Not to exceed 5 percent of any appropriation made available for the current fiscal year for the Department of Commerce in this Act may be transferred between such appropriations, but no such appropriation shall be increased by more than 10 percent by any such transfers:  Provided, That any transfer pursuant to this section shall be treated as a reprogramming of funds under section 505 of this Act and shall not be available for obligation or expenditure except in compliance with the procedures set forth in that section:  Provided further, That the Secretary of Commerce shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance of the acquisition or disposal of any capital asset (including land, structures, and equipment) not specifically provided 
for in this Act or any other law appropriating funds for the Department of Commerce.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the advance-notification and reprogramming procedures are a form of consultation before a federal decision. But the only parties notified are the congressional Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government. The section otherwise only governs transfers of appropriated funds within the Department of Commerce, with no role for states, the public, or any other outside party.
fable.s: the Secretary of Commerce shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance of the acquisition or disposal of any capital asset

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Commerce to notify congressional committees (Committees on Appropriations) regarding fund transfers and asset acquisitions. Congress is considered part of the federal government, so this notification is an intra-governmental process. It does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Commerce shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance of the acquisition or disposal of any capital asset

opus.w: This section lets the Department of Commerce move funds between its appropriations and requires the Secretary to notify the congressional Appropriations Committees beforehand. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so notifying them and following the reprogramming procedures is not participation. No one outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in the decision.
opus.s: the Secretary of Commerce shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance of the acquisition or disposal of any capital asset
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that this is participation because the Secretary must notify the Committees on Appropriations 15 days before acquiring or disposing of capital assets, and transfers must follow the reprogramming procedures in section 505. That fails the definition. The Committees on Appropriations are part of Congress, so they are inside the federal government. Reprogramming procedures happen between the agency and Congress. No state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public is consulted at any point.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Commerce to notify congressional committees regarding capital asset acquisitions or disposals. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this notification is an intra-governmental procedure and does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Commerce shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance of the acquisition or disposal of any capital asset
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying Congress constitutes "participation" because it involves an external check on executive action. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, notifications to congressional committees are intra-governmental communications and do not count as participation with outside parties.
